title: agent-config.yaml
description: Config-as-code for a domain agent. THE source of truth for what an agent-config.yaml may contain: the console's YAML import validates every upload against this file before applying it, and reports the YAML path + line of anything that does not fit. The platform baseline (identity, observability, org-enforced guardrails) is deliberately NOT expressible here — see x-platform-locked.

name.description: Agent / project name. Becomes the project name, so it obeys the same slug rule the wizard's name field does.
name.x-hint: expected lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter or digit.

model.description: Model id. Must additionally be APPROVED in the AI Registry for the importing session's domain — that check is a live registry lookup, not a schema enum.

system_prompt.description: A FILE REFERENCE, never inline prose: a relative .md/.markdown/.txt path inside the app repo, so the instructions are reviewed in a PR and versioned with the agent.
system_prompt.x-hint: expected a relative .md/.markdown/.txt file reference inside the repo (e.g. app/chat_agent/instructions.md), not inline text.

memory.description: Memory retention + isolation. A config may tighten these; the platform's own memory plan is not overridable here.

guardrails.description: Domain-chosen guardrail ids, as a flat list. Each id must be one the console really knows. Org-enforced and domain-enforced guardrails are added by the platform whether or not they appear here — omitting one does NOT switch it off, and attempting to switch one off is rejected (x-platform-locked).

output.description: Optional structured-output contract for the agent's response.

schema.description: A FILE REFERENCE to a committed JSON Schema, same discipline as system_prompt.
schema.x-hint: expected a relative .json file reference inside the repo (e.g. app/chat_agent/response.schema.json).

x-platform-locked.description: Platform-enforced baseline. These keys are owned by the platform and merged on generate; a config that tries to set or override one is REJECTED rather than silently ignored, so an importing builder learns the policy instead of believing the override worked.
x-platform-locked.guardrailBaselineMessage: is a platform-enforced guardrail baseline — an agent-config.yaml may not set or override it. List the guardrails you are ADDING; enforced ones are merged by the platform.
